proposals.summary:
Round 2 leaves 17 split items: roles.primary on 1 unit, roles.secondary on 2, and 14 other fields on one unit each. None is random. Each comes from one of three causes: a rule that two readings both satisfy, a tie-break that is missing, or a page that one coder read and another did not read or could not cite. 16 'must' proposals settle every one. With them, all three coders would code each of the four units the same way:
- Overlord: anti-armour; secondary [support, transport]; Gattling free-aim.
- Atlas: assault, no secondary role; LRM off-screen.
- Marine squad: power-suit and self-repair; flavour [empire].
- Magrider: fast; climb coded; resources [limited-ammo]; 4 abilities with Magburner as channel on a medium cooldown; no magazine on the Halberd; Smoke Screen linked to jam-sensors and fire-countermeasures; high confidence with Census cited.

The biggest single fix is R2-15. It says that 'the sources' means the cited pages plus pages named in uncertain entries. It adds a reading floor and an order for filling the source slots, so codes no longer depend on the cap. 'Should' and 'could' proposals settle the conflicts coders found between two rules:
- 'Assault' against the label 'Frontline assault'
- the rotary 'Gattling Cannon' caught by two tie-breaks
- plasma or cannon
- the MechWarrior title split
- passenger seats and abilities that an upgrade adds
- step-4 bonuses written on the target's side
- secondary roles from roles with no requires
- 'effective against' as a target label
- view buttons against timed buffs
- the trait evidence rules
- PlanetSide 2 range words
- the Generals string file and generals' versions
- casemate with a roof turret
- muzzle velocity
- the sergeant example
- 'count as this' in the rockets tie-break
- active against ultimate
- the cost in overclock-self
- matchup naming

The proposals add no new link kinds, schema fields or validator checks. The three RA3 samples were checked against every proposal and need no fix. They change some codes that coders had agreed on, and each stays agreed:
- The DoW2 missile launcher loses magazine.
- Marine confidence rises to high.
- A sergeant ability and the Overlord add-ons gain upgrade-in-field.
- naval goes onto the Atlas LRM for coder A.

proposals.evidence: Overlord roles.primary split: anti-armour (A, B) against assault (C). All three Generals reports hesitated and each wrote it up as an unclear rule. B-generals: the same question decides the Battlemaster. The MiG's 'Base/Unit Assault' shows that the word names a target, not a job.
proposals.root_cause: The roles list says official words name a role 'only through the role's label or one of its aliases'. It never says whether one word of a two-word label counts. 'Frontline assault' has no aliases. Slash labels are matched by one half (the registry's own example is 'Purpose: Siege').
proposals.target: data/vocab/roles.json (list description); research/registry-notes/games-r3.md (Generals official role lines, Designation bullet)
proposals.change:
(1) roles.json description. OLD: Official words name a role only through the role's label or one of its aliases. NEW: Official words name a role only through the role's whole label or one of its aliases; each half of a slash label (Artillery / siege) counts as a label. One word of a longer label is not enough: 'Assault' alone does not name Frontline assault, so a Purpose such as 'Tank/Structure Assault' names no role.
(2) games-r3.md, Designation bullet, after 'Many entries are phrases that match no role label or alias, and those name no role.' ADD: Entries built on the word Assault (Tank/Structure Assault, Base/Unit Assault) are among them.
proposals.expected: Overlord: step 1 finds no role, and step 4 reads the tooltip's 'Strong vs. vehicles' line. That gives anti-armour for A, B and C (C changes from assault). Secondary step 1 gives nothing either. The Marine squad, Atlas and Magrider do not change: their lines name no role.
proposals.side_effects: The Battlemaster and the MiG also go on to step 4. The RA3 samples do not change ('Anti-Armor', 'anti-vehicle', the IFV by step 4). Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: Overlord secondary split: [siege, support] (A, B) against [anti-armour, siege] (C). All three Generals reports hesitated on siege. 'Strong vs. buildings' is not 'built to break', and the role description (very far, from above, over cover) hardly fits a direct-fire tank. C-generals unclear rule: the Overlord's reach just passes the long edge, so it qualifies, but the Battlemaster, with the same Purpose, does not. A and C filed fit_notes asking for a direct-fire role that breaks structures.
proposals.root_cause: Siege's coding rule ends with 'or a long-range weapon the source says is built to break structures' and never says what counts as that. So any direct-fire gun just past the long edge, with a tooltip line about buildings, becomes siege. That contradicts the next sentence, 'A long-range missile or cannon alone is not siege'.
proposals.change: Replace the source_rule with: A lobbed weapon that reaches long or further, bombs dropped from the air, a deploy mode whose gun reaches long or further and hits an area, or a long-range missile or rocket that the sources say is built mainly to destroy structures (they name structures as its first or only target). A gun aimed straight at targets in view is never siege by that last clause, even when official text calls it strong against buildings: a gun strong against vehicles and buildings gives the anti-armour role. A long-range missile or cannon alone is not siege, and a team that sets up its gun before firing is not deploying.
proposals.expected: Overlord, with R2-01: siege drops. Step 3 gives nothing else, because the Weak vs. line drops anti-infantry from the splash cannons. At step 5, each add-on gives one role: the Propaganda Tower gives support, the Battle Bunker gives transport, and the tower also gives buffer. Roles-list order then gives [support, transport] for A, B and C. All three change. The Atlas does not change: siege already failed there on 'a long-range missile alone'.
proposals.side_effects: Direct-fire tanks with a 'strong vs. buildings' line lose siege, while missile launchers built against bases keep it. The A and C fit_notes asking for a structure-breaker role go to the gap report.

proposals.evidence: Atlas secondary split: [anti-armour] (A, C) against [] (B). A-mech and C-mech hesitated because the role comes only from the LRM's can_target, which the lock-on rule cut down to 'Mechs. C-mech unclear rule: the lock-on rule plus 'it can hit nothing else' gives anti-armour to any LRM whose pages name only 'Mech targets, which looks like an unintended side effect. A-mech's fit_note says the same.
proposals.root_cause: 'It can hit nothing else' reads the coded target list. That list can be short for reasons that say nothing about the weapon's job: can_target step 2 lists only what a lock-on weapon locks onto, and MechWarrior Online has almost nothing but 'Mechs to shoot at.
proposals.change:
(1) roles.secondary. OLD: a source calls it an anti-tank or anti-aircraft weapon, or it can hit nothing else. NEW: a source calls it an anti-tank or anti-aircraft weapon, or it can hit nothing else: the sources say, or the game data shows, that it cannot attack the other kinds of target the game has. A target list that is short only because of can_target step 2 (a lock-on weapon lists what it locks onto), or because the game has few kinds of target, does not count.
(2) roles.primary, step 4. OLD: or if the main weapon can hit nothing else. NEW: or if the main weapon can hit nothing else (as roles.secondary defines it).
proposals.expected: Atlas: the LRM no longer gives anti-armour, and no other weapon gives a role. The AC/20 has no anti-tank wording and no bonus, the SRM has no splash, and siege fails its coding rule. Result: [] for A, B and C (A and C change). The Overlord, Marine squad and Magrider do not change. The RA3 sample IFV does not change either: its source says Tanya's guns attack nothing else.
proposals.side_effects: MechWarrior LRM boats lose an anti-armour role that they had only through the target-list artefact. Lock-on anti-tank and anti-air launchers in other games keep their roles through 'a source calls it an anti-tank or anti-aircraft weapon'. Rebuild docs/fields.md.

proposals.evidence: Atlas LRM split: off-screen (A, B) against medium (C). A-mech unclear rule: the coding rule names 'fires at targets beyond its own sight' as a reason on its own, but the tie-break says a weapon that is short or medium by its reach keeps that band. B-mech: the rules never say whether indirect fire counts as firing beyond its own sight. A-, B- and C-generals: unclear whether an add-on uses the sight figure of the unit that carries it.
proposals.root_cause: The tie-break's 'keeps that band' sentence was written for the first reason (reach past the sight figure), but it reads as overriding every reason. Indirect fire at targets that others spot is not named as an example of the second reason.
proposals.change:
(1) Tie-break long/off-screen. OLD: Check off-screen first, and pick it only for the reasons in its coding rule. A weapon that reaches past its unit's sight but is short or medium by its reach keeps that band. NEW: Check off-screen first, and pick it only for the reasons in its coding rule. Its first reason needs a weapon that is long by its reach: one that reaches past its unit's sight but is short or medium by its reach keeps that band. Its second reason stands on its own, whatever the reach: a weapon the sources say fires indirectly at targets that a teammate or a spotter locks, marks or sees for it fires at targets beyond its own sight.
(2) off-screen source_rule. OLD: reaches past its own unit's sight figure, the figure its sight band uses; NEW: reaches past its own unit's sight figure, the figure its sight band uses (for an add-on or a turret, the unit that carries it);
proposals.expected: Atlas LRM: off-screen for A, B and C. C changes, because the cited MechWarrior Online pages say the LRM fires indirectly at targets that teammates lock or TAG. The Overlord does not change: the Gattling stays off-screen against the Overlord's own figure and the twin cannons stay long.
proposals.side_effects: Indirect-fire weapons that are medium by their reach become off-screen. Off-screen meets siege's requires, but siege's coding rule still turns away long-range missiles. Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: Marine squad body.plan split: power-suit (A, C) against humanoid (B). It also moved flavour_affinity: [empire] against []. All three DoW2 reports hesitated and wrote it up as an unclear rule. There is no tie-break. Power-suit says 'bigger than a soldier' yet 'at small size it is infantry', and the armour-class soldier rule speaks of 'a power suit worn by one soldier (body size small)'. All three body notes already say the marines are power-armoured.
proposals.root_cause: Power-suit's meaning contradicts itself for a suit of one soldier's size, and no tie-break separates powered armour from ordinary body armour.
proposals.change:
(1) power-suit description. OLD: An armoured exosuit, bigger than a soldier. At small size it is infantry; at medium size or bigger it is a walker. NEW: Powered armour, an exosuit or a battlesuit around one pilot. At small size (one soldier's size, such as power armour) it is infantry; at medium size or bigger it is a walker.
(2) New tie-break, terms [humanoid, power-suit]: Power suit when the sources say the soldier wears powered armour, an exosuit or a battlesuit (Space Marines, the PlanetSide 2 MAX, Elementals). Humanoid for a soldier in ordinary body armour or carapace, however heavy. Size and armour class follow their own rules: a suit of one soldier's size is small and light (see Armour classes).
proposals.expected: Marine squad: power-suit for A, B and C (B changes). flavour_affinity then becomes [empire] for all three: Empire scores 2 (blades from the fists, and the power suit) and Soviet scores 1 (assault). The armour class stays light. The other units do not change.
proposals.side_effects: Power-armoured Space Marine and Chaos squads become power-suit and gain an Empire flavour point. Scouts and Guardsmen stay humanoid. Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: Marine squad armour.models split: flat-pool (A) against self-repair (B, C). B and C found a slow health regeneration rate on the Leveling tab, which they read but did not cite. The Guardsmen, Scouts and Shoota Boyz tabs give the same rate. Both coded self-repair and added fit_notes asking the merge pass to decide. Their unclear-rule notes (B-dow2, C-dow2) say the Game-wide list does not mention it. A never read the Leveling tab.
proposals.root_cause: The DoW2 Game-wide list leaves out a shared mechanic. One coder applied the armour-model rule (a model counts even when every unit of its kind shares it), and one never saw the mechanic.
proposals.target: research/registry-notes/games-r5.md: Game-wide mechanics, Dawn of War II, new bullet after Melee
proposals.change: ADD bullet: - **Health regeneration** (armour model self-repair): every infantry unit's Leveling tab lists a slow health regeneration rate (the Tactical Marines, Guardsmen, Scouts and Shoota Boyz tabs checked in pilot round 2 give the same rate), and veterancy raises it. It belongs to the unit, so code self-repair on every unit whose Leveling tab lists a rate, as the armour-models rule asks for a model every unit of its kind shares; say in armour.notes that it is slow and shared. A unit whose tab lists none has no self-repair. Read the Leveling tab for this; no fit_note is needed.
proposals.expected: Marine squad: [self-repair] for A, B and C (A changes; B and C drop their fit_notes). The other units do not change.
proposals.side_effects: Every DoW2 infantry squad whose tab lists a rate gets self-repair, so flat-pool disappears for them. If Mustafa or the merge pass would rather leave base regeneration off, the same bullet can say 'leave it off and mention it in armour.notes'. Either version settles the split.

proposals.evidence: Magrider speed split: fast (A, C) against very-fast (B). All three PlanetSide 2 reports hesitated: no page gives a speed for any PS2 vehicle. Against the 6.5 m/s sprint reference, a battle tank lands near the 2.5 edge (B: 'near 2.5 times'; C: the edge is about 58.5 km/h). The registry note had warned of this.
proposals.root_cause: 'With nothing usable, judge from figures for neighbouring units or from footage' has no rule for a judgement that lands on an edge, although a ratio on an edge has one.
proposals.change: OLD: With nothing usable, judge from figures for neighbouring units or from footage, and add an uncertain entry for mobility/speed. NEW: With nothing usable, judge from figures for neighbouring units or from footage, and add an uncertain entry for mobility/speed. A judgement that lands near an edge, with no figure or comparison that puts it clearly past, takes the band nearer medium, as a ratio on an edge does.
proposals.expected: Magrider: fast for A, B and C (B changes). The other units have figures and do not change.
proposals.side_effects: PS2 tanks with no speed figure land on fast unless a source says they are clearly faster. That shooter vehicles bunch together under method A is decision 2C, and this proposal does not reopen it.

proposals.evidence: Magrider resources split: [limited-ammo] (A) against [limited-ammo, fuel] (B, C); all three filed fit_notes. A second split hides inside the measured union, on the Magburner's cooldown: medium (A, C) against none (B, who read it as 'held back only by a stock'). Hesitations: A-, B- and C-ps2 on resources; B-ps2 and C-ps2 on cooldown; C-ps2 unclear rule on abilities with a fuel gauge.
proposals.root_cause: Fuel (a gauge that refills on the ground or at a pad) and the cooldown rule (a stock gives no band) were written for jets and munitions. A boost's own small tank that refills by itself fits neither, so it can be read as a resource, as a stock or as a cooldown.
proposals.change:
(1) fuel. OLD: Flight or boost time drains a gauge that refills on the ground or at a pad. NEW: Flight or boost time drains a gauge that refills on the ground or at a pad. A gauge that only one ability draws on and that refills on its own is that ability's cooldown, not fuel (see Cooldown bands).
(2) cooldown-bands description, after 'An ability held back only by a stock, such as Company of Heroes munitions or the unit's energy, has no band unless the source also gives a cooldown.' ADD: A gauge that only this ability draws on and that refills on its own (a boost's own fuel tank) is its cooldown, not a stock: band the time it takes to refill from empty.
proposals.expected: Magrider: resources [limited-ammo] for A, B and C (B and C drop fuel). The Magburner's cooldown is medium for all three, banded from the time to refill from empty at rank 1 (B adds it). Recharge keeps fire-countermeasures and its fit_note. The Atlas keeps heat, because many weapons share that gauge.
proposals.side_effects: Boosts and afterburners with their own refilling meter get a cooldown band and no fuel. Jetpacks and aircraft that refill on landing keep fuel. Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: Magburner kind split: channel (A, B) against active (C). A based channel on the Afterburner page, which says the boost stops when the key is let go; A read it but did not cite it. B based it on the Magburner page's 'press and hold'. C read the same 'press and hold' but chose active, because the tie-break needs the source to say the effect stops on release (C-ps2 hesitation). A-ps2 asked in an unclear-rule note whether uncited pages count.
proposals.root_cause: The tie-break asks for words about letting go, while sources usually say only 'hold the key'. Channel's own meaning, 'Hold to keep it going', already covers that.
proposals.change: OLD: Pick channel only when the source says the effect stops as soon as you let go, move or are interrupted. A timed action that runs to its end on its own is active. NEW: Pick channel when the source says you hold the key to keep the effect going (press and hold), or that it stops as soon as you let go, move or are interrupted. A timed action that runs to its end on its own is active.
proposals.expected: Magburner: channel for A, B and C (C changes). No other round-2 unit has a held ability.
proposals.side_effects: None known. Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: Magrider ability count split: 5 (A, B) against 4 (C). A and B recorded Multi-directional Exhaust as a passive with no pattern; their gaps say no pattern fits a pick that reshapes another ability. C put it in notes as an extension of strafing. A-ps2 unclear rule: a passive pick that changes another ability.
proposals.root_cause: The rule 'add a passive when the source names the effect and it adds a mechanic' does not say whether changing how another ability works counts as a mechanic of its own.
proposals.change: After 'Leave out passives that only change numbers (more armour, faster reload, less sway), and note them in the matching field's notes.' ADD: A pick, upgrade or perk that changes how one of the unit's other abilities or weapons works (a boost that refills faster and can also steer sideways) is not an entry of its own either: say what it changes, and that it is a pick, in that ability's or weapon's summary.
proposals.expected: Magrider: A and B move Multi-directional Exhaust into the Magburner's summary, so they go from 5 abilities to 4 and lose the passive. C does not change. With R2-09, abilities.kind becomes {active, channel} for all three. The other units do not change.
proposals.side_effects: Picks and upgrades that change an existing ability stay out of abilities in every game. The gap report can still ask for a dash variant that steers sideways.

proposals.evidence: Magrider trait split: magazine on the E540 Halberd (B only). B's reason: the Halberd's own page, which B read but did not cite, names its long reload as a weakness. Single-shot weapons troubled coders elsewhere too. All three DoW2 reports hesitated on the one-missile launcher; C-dow2: 'one missile per reload is an odd fit for a set number of shots'. A-ps2 and C-ps2 hesitated on the Supernova's quick reload (C-ps2 unclear rule).
proposals.root_cause: Magazine ('a set number of shots, then reload') does not say whether one shot per reload counts. For a single-shot weapon the reload is simply its rate of fire, so whether a page happens to mention it decides the trait.
proposals.change: APPEND to the source_rule: A weapon that holds one shot per reload (a single-shot launcher or cannon) never gets it for that reload: its reload is its rate of fire, so say in the summary how long it takes.
proposals.expected: Magrider: the Halberd is [splash] for A, B and C (B drops magazine). The Supernova and Perihelion do not change. Marine squad: the missile launcher drops magazine for A, B and C, so the three agree on a new value and their hesitations go. Overlord: the twin cannons stay without magazine, since their two-shot clip appears only in stats. The Atlas does not change. RA3 sample: the IFV's Javelin pod fires a burst and then reloads, so it keeps magazine.
proposals.side_effects: Single-shot launchers and cannons lose magazine in every game. Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: Magrider traits split: [boost, crush, climb] (A, B, each with two atypicals) against [boost, crush] (C, with a fit_note asking for climb). A-ps2 and B-ps2 hesitated. Climb is banned for hover, and the hover type 'avoids steep slopes'. But the vocabularies say a real unit that breaks a rule is recorded as it is and listed as atypical.
proposals.root_cause: Climb has no coding rule. So coders differ on whether a banned trait that the source shows is coded and listed as atypical, or left to notes.
proposals.change: ADD source_rule: Code it when the sources show the unit going up walls, cliffs or buildings that stop other units of its kind, however it does it (legs, claws, hover thrust). Where the trait's rules leave out the unit's class or mobility, code it anyway; the validator lists the break as atypical, which is evidence for relaxing the rule.
proposals.expected: Magrider: [boost, crush, climb] for A, B and C. C adds climb and so gets the two climb atypicals. The other units do not change.
proposals.side_effects: Climb on hover units is listed as atypical, which gives the gap report evidence. Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: Magrider patterns split on Smoke Screen: [jam-sensors, fire-countermeasures] (A, C) against [lay-smoke, jam-sensors] (B). C read the Smoke Screen page: missiles already locked on lose their target, and the smoke is light and only hard to see through. B never read that page. A-, B- and C-ps2 all hesitated.
proposals.root_cause: The ECM example under Pattern links does not say which part of 'hides you and stops locks' is jam-sensors and which is fire-countermeasures. It also never says when smoke counts as lay-smoke. And this PlanetSide 2 pick, shared by many vehicles, is missing from the registry's list of vehicle slot picks.
proposals.target: research/registry-notes/games-r6.md (PlanetSide 2 Game-wide mechanics, Vehicle slot picks); scripts/build-docs.mjs (Conventions, Pattern links)
proposals.change:
(1) games-r6.md, Vehicle slot picks bullet, after 'Flares that break locks link fire-countermeasures.' ADD: Smoke Screen, which for a few seconds hides the vehicle and friendly vehicles near it from enemy minimap detection, blocks new lock-ons and makes missiles already locked on lose their target (its own wiki page), links jam-sensors and fire-countermeasures. Its smoke is thin, so it links no lay-smoke.
(2) build-docs.mjs, Pattern links, after the sentence ending 'links `jam-sensors` and `fire-countermeasures`.' ADD: Blocking new locks is part of `jam-sensors`; add `fire-countermeasures` only when the sources say it also breaks a lock already made or defeats missiles in flight. Smoke links `lay-smoke` only when the sources say it blocks sight or aim.
proposals.expected: Magrider: Smoke Screen is [jam-sensors, fire-countermeasures] for A, B and C (B changes). Recharge stays [fire-countermeasures]. The other units do not change.
proposals.side_effects: Every PS2 vehicle that carries Smoke Screen gets the same pair. Rebuild docs/fields.md.

proposals.evidence: Magrider confidence split: high (A, C, who cited Census) against medium (B, who cited only wiki pages). Seven reports hesitated on confidence: A-, B- and C-dow2, B- and C-generals, A-mech and B-ps2. The registry names the DoW2 box description and the PS2 infobox Description field as copies of in-game text. But 'high' asks for 'a faithful copy that says what it copies', and these pages never say so. B-ps2 unclear rule: should the registry's word be enough?
proposals.root_cause: Confidence and the roles list define official text read through a copy differently. Roles accept the registry's word on which infobox fields copy in-game text. Confidence asks the page itself to say so.
proposals.change: OLD: The sources include official text about the unit, read directly or through a faithful copy that says what it copies, or pages from two different established sites that each describe the unit and agree. NEW: The cited sources include official text about the unit, read directly or through a faithful copy: a page that says what it copies, or an infobox field the game's registry note names as a copy of in-game text (the Dawn of War II unit box's description, the PlanetSide 2 Wiki's Description field). Or they include pages from two different established sites that each describe the unit and agree. (The rest of the term stays as it is.)
proposals.expected: Magrider: high for A, B and C (B changes; its cited Magrider/Main page carries the Description field). Marine squad: high for A, B and C (all three change from medium, because the cited unit page carries the box description, so they still agree). The Overlord and Atlas stay high.
proposals.side_effects: More units reach high on a single site where the registry names a copied field. The DoW2 note's own check, whether the box field really copies the tooltip, goes to the gap report. Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: 10 of 12 reports hesitated on sources. 86 of 166 uncertain entries rest on pages read but not cited, and every report has some. B-dow2 and C-dow2 unclear rules: damage step 4 and the rockets or guided missiles tie-break say 'the sources cited', while can_target step 3, magazine, splash and roles say just 'the sources'. A-ps2 asked the same about the channel tie-break. Six of the 17 split items trace to this: Magrider sources.kind and confidence (B cited the resistance page instead of Census), Magrider ability kind (C would not use an uncited page), and Marine armour.models and Magrider patterns (a page one coder never read).
proposals.root_cause: The sources rule lets a band rest on an uncited page (marked uncertain) but says nothing about a term, and two rules limit themselves to cited pages. So which pages fill the slots, and which pages a coder happened to read, change the codes. Nothing says which page takes a slot first.
proposals.target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json (sources[]; armament[].damage step 4; armament[].delivery; armament[].can_target step 3); data/vocab/weapon-families.json (tie-break rockets/guided-missiles); data/vocab/range-bands.json (tie-break short/medium/long)
proposals.change:
(1) sources[] description, NEW: The pages this entry rests on. Wherever a field rule says the sources, it means these cited pages together with every page read for this unit that an uncertain entry names (title and site, or its URL) and says what it shows. Every rule reads that same set; any code that rests only on an uncited page gets an uncertain entry at its own path. Confidence counts only the cited pages. Read every tab or sub-page of the unit's own page, and the page of each of its weapons, abilities and loadout picks where the site has one. Fill the slots in this order: an official page about the unit when one was read (see Source kinds); the page that lists the unit's weapons one by one, when its weapons change by passenger, mode or loadout; then the pages most of the entry rests on, a mechanic's own page first when it gives a figure the entry uses.
(2) Damage step 4. OLD: and the sources cited for this unit give. NEW: and the sources give.
(3) Delivery. OLD: as the cited sources describe it. NEW: as the sources describe it.
(4) can_target step 3. OLD: plus any kind another cited source says it hurts. NEW: plus any kind another source says it hurts.
(5) Rockets or guided missiles tie-break. OLD: Guided missiles only when the sources cited for the unit say. NEW: Guided missiles only when the sources say.
(6) Range tie-break. OLD: from its figure where a cited page or the registry gives one. NEW: from its figure where a source or the registry gives one.
proposals.expected:
Magrider: B cites the Census entry (official) first, so sources.kind is {official, wiki} for all three (B changes). B reads the Smoke Screen page under the reading floor, though R2-13 settles that anyway. The Magburner is channel for all three, with R2-09.
Marine squad: A reads the Leveling tab (R2-06 settles it anyway). All three cite the Retribution manual first, so sources.kind is {official, wiki} for all three; all change and still agree. The missile launcher's anti-armour role stays for all three, now on the rule's own terms.
Overlord and Atlas: no official page was read (the MUL refused every request), so their citations stay. Their codes stand: the Atlas ranges and autocannon family, and the Gattling family.
proposals.side_effects: The cap (3 or 5) no longer changes any code. It now changes only confidence and what the copy-check sees. Uncited pages are not copy-checked, so coders' own checks are still needed. A cited PDF manual, like the DoW2 one, cannot be copy-checked either. A coder who reads raw game data files can set new terms from them: B and C saw in Generals' 1.04 Weapon.ini that the Overlord's blast hurts allies, a friendly-fire trait nobody coded. R2-27 settles that for Generals. Rebuild docs/fields.md and docs/vocabularies.md.

proposals.evidence: All three MechWarrior reports wrote up unclear rules on 'the newest counted title'. How it plays comes from MechWarrior 5: Clans where its pages cover the 'Mech, otherwise from MechWarrior Online: whether a weapon locks on, fires one shell or a burst, or fires indirectly, and what happens when it dies. Kinds of target come from all counted titles together: the tabletop has infantry, VTOLs (low air) and naval vessels, so 'Mech weapons list them where their own rules allow. So the Atlas's centre-torso lasers face backwards; an Inner Sphere autocannon that MechWarrior Online fires as one shell per shot is a cannon; LRMs lock on and also fire indirectly; SRMs that MechWarrior Online calls non-locking are rockets with no homing trait, and the tabletop's self-guided wording goes in notes. OLD: In a shooter it is the weapon the driver seat has selected at spawn (its first fire button); NEW: In a shooter it is the weapon the driver seat has selected at spawn (its first fire button), or, where players build their own fire groups and no source gives the spawn default, the weapon that the registry's design source lists first (MechWarrior: the BattleTechWiki infobox);

for_mustafa.question: Source cap: keep 3 or raise to 5?
for_mustafa.evidence:
- All 12 reports used all three slots, and 10 of 12 said in a sources hesitation that the cap forced a trade-off.
- 86 of 166 uncertain entries (52%) rest on pages that were read but left uncited. Every report has some, from 2 to 13 per report.
- In all 12 reports, codes in measured fields rest on such pages: the DoW2 missile launcher's anti-armour role and magazine (3 of 3), the Marine squad's self-repair (2), all four Atlas weapon ranges and the autocannon family (3 of 3), the Overlord's Gattling family (3 of 3), the Magburner's kind (2), the Halberd's magazine (1) and Smoke Screen's countermeasures (1).
- 4 of 12 reports left an official page uncited for lack of room: the three DoW2 manuals and the PS2 Census entry. Each said citing it would have made confidence high. The Census case is the Magrider's confidence and source-kind split.
- 6 of the 17 split items trace to a page that one coder read but did not cite, or did not read at all.

With R2-15 (the sources means cited pages plus pages named in uncertain entries, and official pages fill the first slot), a cap of 3 no longer changes any round-2 code. It then changes only confidence and what the copy-check and the checker see. A cap of 5 would let the DoW2 manual, the Census entry and the MechWarrior weapon pages be cited and copy-checked; the DoW2 manual is a PDF, though, which the copy-check cannot read.
